Hi Ellen / Tom / procurement team —

Thanks — I drafted a sequencing plan and a short mutual action plan (MAP) that aligns the evaluation sprint milestones with contract and procurement gates. High level summary below; attached is a MAP workbook that you can drop into your procurement tracker (Redwood-MAP-20280607.xlsx).

Proposed timeline (target earliest):
- Week 0 (Sign MSA): target signature 2028-06-14 — legal has confirmed standard MSA template is acceptable to SynthMed legal in principle.
- Days 1–5 after MSA (DPA redlines): we’ll prioritize DPA review; estimated 3–5 business days if there are only a couple of narrow data residency clauses.
- Day 6 (Order form ready): procurement completes order form and issues PO — requires signed MSA + DPA redline concurrence.
- Day 7 (Onramp start): Redwood dedicates capacity for the 3-week evaluation sprint.

Fallbacks & mitigations:
- If DPA redlines take longer than 7 business days, we can run a limited ‘sandbox eval’ under an interim data handling attestation (no PHI, restricted dataset) while the DPA finalizes. This preserves momentum but does not allow production data.
- We can pre-stage order form to be finalized pending DPA confirmation (procurement provides conditional PO issuance).

Action items (for clarity):
1) SynthMed legal to send any DPA redlines by 2028-06-10 to hit the earliest start.
2) Redwood legal (cc’d if needed) will review and return redlines within 48–72 hours for initial cycles.
3) Procurement to confirm PO approval cadence and any internal hold points.
4) Neha to schedule kickoff and define evaluation acceptance criteria (SLOs & test prompts).

Attachments: Redwood-MAP-20280607.xlsx (MAP workbook with milestone dates and owners).

Sounds tight but feasible if we keep the DPA window narrow — happy to walk through the MAP with procurement.
